answer: Each agent can earn influence only through long-lived, randomly assigned work threads whose outputs are checked by independent peers selected from a public beacon. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across many Sybils does not multiply trust; each thread must still be completed and validated. The attacker must therefore fund repeated work, wait for reputation to accumulate, and risk losing bonded stake when peers catch fabricated results—a costly way to grow a fake garden of identities.
